## Owner's choice: measure first, then fix only what is still bad
A QA audit (before the Nov 23 speed PRs #318–#322 and later changes) reported three Home problems. Use skill `measure-speed` and the memory-free setup in AGENTS.md: production build (`npm run qa:server` builds `.next-qa`), seeded QA workspace with realistic synthetic volume (e.g. 10+ accounts, several thousand transactions, an artifact card on Home, widgets customized) plus an empty workspace. PR #335 (merged) moved the first-run checklist to its own card and #333 added a Cash flow empty state. Reproduce with the spec and with a PerformanceObserver (`layout-shift` entries with `sources`) to name the elements that move and when (streamed Suspense boundaries, widget skeletons with the wrong height, fonts, images, the masonry grid re-flowing). Fix at the source — e.g. skeletons that reserve the real height, or the grid not re-flowing when a late widget arrives — so the spec passes reliably (`--repeat-each=5`).
2. **Slow page opens.** Live (owner's desktop app, data volume unknown) Home took 18.4 s and Settings 13.9 s to show their heading on recheck, with load events >15 s; Transactions 1.3 s. QA measured Home 2.7 s on a first context, ~0.5 s after. Measure Home and Settings heading time and server response time on the seeded QA workspace, cold and warm. If either is slow, trace which server reads dominate (server timing / logs) and fix the slow read. Also check startup of background jobs (`lib/scheduler.ts`) competing with the first request. If they are fast on QA, say so with numbers and note what could make the live desktop slower (data size, first start after update with migrations/backup) — do not guess-fix.
3. **A hidden artifact card came back after reload.** In one full e2e run on 2026-11-25, `e2e/artifact-home.gated.spec.ts` "an artifact card previews natively, goes on Home at its size, reacts to its control and leaves with the artifact": after hiding the card and reloading, it was still on Home — possibly a Home layout save lost or raced (the dev server was still starting). Try to reproduce (`--repeat-each=10`, and under load). If you find a lost/raced layout write (e.g. two concurrent saves of the home layout with last-write-wins, or a save fired before hydration), fix it at the source and add a test where it belongs (`lib/` unit test for the merge/version logic, or extend the spec).

# Browser tests

Playwright tests run against the separate test backend (Docker project `moneo-qa`, `.env.qa`) and this checkout's app on http://localhost:3100. The config starts the app with `npm run qa:server` (or a production build with `E2E_PRODUCTION_BUILD=1`) unless it is already running.

## Setup

1. Create the test backend once (and after pulling new migrations): `npm run setup -- --qa`.
2. Create the QA user and save its session: `npm run qa:auth`. Its login is stored in `.env.qa` as `E2E_USER_EMAIL`/`E2E_USER_PASSWORD`, and its session in `e2e/.auth.json` (or set `E2E_STORAGE_STATE`).
3. Before a full run, empty its workspace: `npm run qa:reset`.

The whole test backend is disposable: `docker compose -p moneo-qa down -v` and step 1 start it fresh. The owner's `moneo` project is never touched.

Tests never use the owner's workspace. Every spec runs with the saved QA session and an `x-moneo-test` header; with that header the app refuses a request that has no valid session instead of signing the owner in (`proxy.ts`). Before any spec runs, `e2e/global-setup.ts` checks that the server under test does this, so an older or foreign server on the port stops the run.

## Running

```sh
npm run test:e2e -- --workers=1
```

Use one worker: several specs change the same QA workspace and its preferences. The QA server builds into `.next-qa`, so it can run beside `npm run dev`.

## Kinds of specs

- `*.smoke.spec.ts` and `*.mocked.spec.ts` stub or skip the backend. Against a configured backend they still need the QA session, like every spec.
- `*.gated.spec.ts` need the backend. Most use the QA session; others create disposable users with the service key, sign them in by session cookie, and remove them in `finally`. If interrupted, their IDs are left in ignored `.qa/` files for cleanup.
- `*.provider.spec.ts` call the real AI model, so they cost money. They run only with `E2E_REAL_AI=1`; `npm run test:e2e` leaves them out.
- `review-runtime.config.ts` and `review-investigation.config.ts` run the real Workflow engine against local synthetic database and model servers (ports 3040/3041), including a server restart mid-review: `npx playwright test --config e2e/review-runtime.config.ts`.

## Pull-request CI

The `browser` job in `.github/workflows/ci.yml` runs on every pull request. It starts its own disposable `moneo-qa` backend on the runner (`npm run setup -- --qa`, with the same retry as the `database` job), creates the QA user (`npm run qa:auth`), builds this checkout and serves it on port 3100 against `.env.qa` with AI, bank and Scalable access off (`E2E_PRODUCTION_BUILD=1`, see `scripts/qa-server.mjs`), then runs one worker with one retry over a bounded set of specs: `net-worth.gated.spec.ts` (accepting a cash-machine proposal card once even when double-clicked, dismissing one without applying it, and checking both after a reload; proposal cards have no undo, so none is tested) and `import-journey.mocked.spec.ts`. A failure fails the job and uploads `test-results/` (a trace and screenshot per failed test) as the `browser-failures` artifact for 7 days. The runner and its backend are discarded afterwards, and the specs only create synthetic rows, so the artifact holds no owner data or credentials. The specs refuse any server that would sign tests in as the owner (`e2e/global-setup.ts`).

To reproduce a CI failure locally, follow Setup, make sure nothing else is serving port 3100, and run:

```sh
E2E_PRODUCTION_BUILD=1 npx playwright test --workers=1 e2e/net-worth.gated.spec.ts e2e/import-journey.mocked.spec.ts
npx playwright show-trace test-results/<failed test folder>/trace.zip
```

## Nightly

`npm run qa:nightly -- --install` schedules the whole suite for 03:00 every day (a Windows scheduled task that starts as soon as possible if the PC was off). It runs every spec twice on a production build of `origin/main`, in its own worktree in `~/.moneo/nightly`, and keeps one GitHub issue, "Nightly browser suite is failing", up to date. A night with Docker off or port 3100 busy is skipped quietly; the log is `~/.moneo/nightly.log`.

A skipped spec is not a pass: it means a prerequisite (backend, QA session, service key) is missing.

## Scalable

`scalable-trading.provider.spec.ts` drives chat against a local stand-in for Scalable's MCP server (`e2e/mocks/scalable-mcp.mjs`, made-up data) with the real AI model. Start `npm run qa:server` with `SCALABLE_MCP_ORIGIN=http://127.0.0.1:3043` (and the AI key in `.env.qa`) and run the spec with the same variable and `E2E_REAL_AI=1`; the spec starts the stand-in, adds a Scalable connection to the QA workspace and removes it afterwards. It checks that an order is previewed on a card and sent only when the card is tapped, once, and that read-only access is told it can't trade.

# Measure speed before and after

Every change should leave Moneo as fast as before or faster. Measure it; never guess. A PR that only changes docs (`*.md`, `docs/`) skips this and writes "No runtime change" under Speed.

Everything runs against the QA backend, never port 3000, on production builds: `next dev` compiles each page on its first visit and makes everything look slow.

## 1. Two builds

- **After:** this checkout. `QA_PORT=3101 npm run qa:server -- --production` in the background.
- **Before:** the PR's base in its own worktree: `git worktree add ../moneo-speed-base origin/main`, then in it `npm ci`, `npm run setup -- --qa` (copies `.env.qa`) and `QA_PORT=3102 npm run qa:server -- --production` in the background.

Both use the same QA workspace, so they see the same data. Each is ready when `curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" -H "x-moneo-test: 1" http://localhost:<port>/api/health` prints 401 or 200. Run `npm run qa:auth` if the session is older than an hour.

Set up the data the change needs the way the nearest spec in `e2e/` does, through the app. An empty page measures an empty page.

## 2. Opening the app

`node scripts/perf-pages.mjs 5 before=http://localhost:3102 after=http://localhost:3101`

It loads every main page cold on desktop and mobile, the two builds interleaved run by run so machine noise hits both alike, and prints the medians: TTFB, first paint, LCP, time until the heading shows, layout shift, long tasks and JS KB. The full results are in `.qa/perf-before.json` and `.qa/perf-after.json`.

## 3. What the change touches

Time the action the change affects, from the owner's tap until its result shows: opening a panel, an import, accepting a card, a sync, a chat answer. Use Playwright against both ports, one warm-up and then at least 5 runs each, and take the median.

Mock AI, bank and Scalable with `page.route`, the way `e2e/*.mocked.spec.ts` does, so nothing costs money and the number is Moneo's own time, not the provider's. `scripts/perf-interactions.mjs` makes real AI calls: run it only when the owner asks.

For work with no screen (a workflow step, a `lib/` function), time it with a small script against the QA backend, both checkouts, same runs and median.

## 4. Read the numbers

A slowdown is a median more than 10% **and** more than 50 ms worse, or more JS on a page. Anything smaller is noise; when in doubt, run again.

A slowdown means this change made Moneo slower. Find the cause (a trace with `--trace on`, the Network tab, the React Profiler) and fix it before opening the PR, then measure again. If the extra time cannot be avoided, say in the PR what costs it and why, and ask the owner.

## 5. Hand over

Add this to the PR description:

```markdown
## Speed

Production builds on QA data, median of 5 runs. Before: `<base sha>`. After: `<head sha>`.

| What | Before | After | Change |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Open Home, desktop (heading shows) | 640 ms | 610 ms | −5% |
| Open Home, mobile | 820 ms | 800 ms | −2% |
| Accept a cash card (tap → new balance) | 310 ms | 290 ms | −6% |
```

List Home, every page the change touches and the action from step 3. Put any slowdown first, with its cause.

## 6. Clean up

Stop only the servers you started, found by port and checkout path, never by name. Remove the base worktree with `git worktree remove ../moneo-speed-base`.

input.body:
Follows up the QA audit's three Home problems. I measured each one first. Only the third one reproduced, and its cause was in the spec, not the app.

## 3. A hidden artifact card came back after reload: fixed (spec race)

I reproduced it once in 9 runs of `artifact-home.gated.spec.ts` ("previews natively…"), on freshly started dev servers with every CPU core busy. In the failed run's trace, the hide's layout-save server action started at 39.791 s. The spec's `page.reload()` followed 49 ms later and aborted it (status −1). The reload then read the old layout. The spec's `page.waitForLoadState("networkidle")` returned at once because the page had already reached that state, so it never waited for the save. The app saved correctly: there was no lost or concurrent layout write, and the versioned update in `app/dashboard-actions.ts` behaves as intended.

Fix: before reloading, the spec now polls `dashboard_layouts` until the card key is gone. If a real save were ever lost, this check still fails. `home-dashboard.gated.spec.ts` already waits for its saves (`saved(page)`).

After the fix the test passed 12/12 under the same load on cold dev servers and 5/5 on a production build. Before the fix, 1 of 9 failed.

## 1. Home layout shift: did not reproduce

`home-performance.gated.spec.ts` passed 5/5 on a production build and 5/5 on the dev server with seeded data. It also passed in a full 58-spec run on the dev server, which is the state the audit measured in. CLS medians (1280×720):

| Workspace | CLS (median of 5) | Largest shift |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Seeded (12 accounts, 6,000 transactions, artifact card, custom sizes), production | 0.025 | Goals widget appears below the fold |
| Seeded, very first load after seeding | 0.034 | "Waiting for you" grows after recurring detection refreshes the page |
| Seeded, dev server | 0.000 | none |
| Empty workspace | 0.000 | none |

PR #335 and #333 landed after the 0.26 measurement and probably fixed it. No code change.

## 2. Slow page opens: fast on QA

Production build, seeded QA workspace, median of 5 (6 for cold), 1280×720:

| What | TTFB | Heading | LCP |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Home, first request after server start | 297 ms | 494 ms | 1,772 ms |
| Home, warm | 19 ms | 172 ms | 1,116 ms |
| Home, while the first scheduled jobs run (+60 s) | 16 ms | 163 ms | 1,108 ms |
| Settings, first request after server start | 218 ms | 402 ms | 628 ms |
| Settings, warm | 14 ms | 83 ms | 152 ms |
| Settings, while scheduled jobs run | 13 ms | 109 ms | 172 ms |
| Home, empty workspace | 15 ms | 126 ms | 452 ms |

These do not explain the live desktop's 18.4 s Home and 13.9 s Settings. I changed nothing for them. Things QA cannot reproduce that could make the desktop slower:

- **First start after an update:** migrations run after the automatic `pre-upgrade` backup.
- **Real AI connections:** with a Claude plan, `claudeAccount()` runs `claude auth status` with a 20 s timeout. Settings waits for it before its heading. On Home it only gates the grid, through `aiConfigured()` → `loadFirstRun`. Here the bundled CLI answered in about 1.1 s cold and 0.3 s warm.
- **Scheduled jobs:** with a working AI key, the jobs started 60 s after launch (agent backlog, bank and Scalable sync) do real work. With QA's placeholder key they fail fast.
- **Unknown data size:** the owner's data volume is not known.

A next step is timing on the desktop app itself (server timing for `requireWorkspace`, `chatgptStatus`, `claudeAccount`).

## Also seen

In the full run, `import-control.gated.spec.ts` failed once in its own `finally` cleanup with `PostgresError: deadlock detected` while deleting the disposable user's rows. This is unrelated to this change.

## Speed

No runtime change: only `e2e/artifact-home.gated.spec.ts` changed, so before and after are the same build (`0d3d62ce`). The production-build medians are in the tables above.

## Checks

`npm test`, `npm run lint`, `npm run typecheck`, `npm run build` and `npm run check:bundle` pass. On a production build, the artifact-home test passed 5/5 and the Home performance spec passed 5/5. On cold dev servers under full CPU load, the artifact-home test passed 12/12.
